title: Pin today's anchor-less thread markup with golden tests
description:
Add characterisation (golden) tests in tests/ that pin the EXACT string renderThread() in src/thread.js returns today for threads with no anchor, so any later change that alters anchor-less output fails the suite. Do not change src/thread.js behaviour in this ticket. Golden strings are captured from the current implementation (today: `
${body}
`), covering several bodies: a plain word, an empty string, a body containing HTML-special characters (&, <, >, quotes) — the current output does NOT escape them and that is what is pinned — and a multi-line body. Anchor-less means the input object has no `anchor` property, or `anchor` is undefined or null. Tests run with `node --test tests`.

acceptanceCriteria.text:
For each of the bodies 'x', '', 'a & "q" \'s\'' and 'line1\nline2', renderThread({ body }) is strictly equal (===) to the exact golden string '
' + body + '
' recorded from today's implementation
acceptanceCriteria.serves: The current anchor-less output is protected by tests so a later change cannot silently alter it

acceptanceCriteria.text:
renderThread({ body: 'x', anchor: undefined }) and renderThread({ body: 'x', anchor: null }) are each strictly equal to '
x
'
acceptanceCriteria.serves: The current anchor-less output is protected by tests so a later change cannot silently alter it

acceptanceCriteria: The golden tests live under tests/ and pass when run with `node --test tests` against the unmodified src/thread.js
src/thread.js is not modified by this ticket
seamsNote: tests only; renderThread() is a pure string function and this ticket writes no state another code path reads.
entrypointsNote: adds no CLI command and no workflow; tests run via the existing `node --test tests` command.
rationale: The PRD requires the anchor-less output be protected by tests; characterisation tests must capture today's output BEFORE the renderer is changed, so pinning is its own behaviour (regression guard) landed first, separate from the new chip behaviour.

title: Render an anchor chip on anchored comment threads
description: Extend renderThread() in src/thread.js (the only renderer — do not add a second one) so a thread object with a non-empty string `anchor` (the anchor's name, e.g. 'L42') renders a chip naming that anchor inside the thread markup: an element with class "anchor-chip" whose text content is the anchor name, placed inside the <div class="thread"> container alongside the body. Threads with no anchor (property absent, undefined or null) must keep returning the exact same string as today; the golden tests from t-001 must stay green unchanged. Creating or editing anchors is out of scope. Visual appearance of the chip ('small') is judged at Verify.

acceptanceCriteria.text: renderThread({ body: 'x', anchor: 'L42' }) returns markup containing exactly one element with class "anchor-chip" whose text content is 'L42'
acceptanceCriteria.serves: An anchored thread renders a chip naming its anchor

acceptanceCriteria.text: The anchor-chip element is inside the outer <div class="thread"> element, and the anchored output still contains the body text 'x' inside that same container
acceptanceCriteria.serves: An anchored thread renders a chip naming its anchor

acceptanceCriteria.text: Different anchors produce chips naming each: renderThread({ body: 'x', anchor: 'L7' }) contains an anchor-chip with text 'L7' and does not contain 'L42'
acceptanceCriteria.serves: An anchored thread renders a chip naming its anchor

acceptanceCriteria.text:
renderThread({ body: 'x' }), renderThread({ body: 'x', anchor: undefined }) and renderThread({ body: 'x', anchor: null }) each still return exactly '
x
' and contain no 'anchor-chip'
acceptanceCriteria.serves: An anchor-less thread renders byte-identically to today

acceptanceCriteria.text: All golden tests added by t-001 pass unmodified under `node --test tests`
acceptanceCriteria.serves: The current anchor-less output is protected by tests so a later change cannot silently alter it

seamsNote: renderThread() is a pure renderer returning a string from its argument; it writes no state that another code path in this repo reads.
entrypointsNote: adds no CLI command and no workflow; tests run via the existing `node --test tests` command.
rationale: This is the single new user-observable behaviour (the chip). It depends on t-001 because it must be built against the golden tests that pin today's anchor-less output, which are the regression guard for this exact change; building it first would let the pinned output be captured after the renderer changed.
